title: Prove one local rank-5 deletion per FULL lifts the selected complex invoice to the BIT saving (no new κ)
body:
## Result

**Finite exact certificate on an accounting relaxation. No new κ; the selected frontier is unchanged.** This result is produced by Nick Petalas.

On the authenticated selected #5599 P104 invoice (`scripts/export_selected_invoice.py` at `19fdb086e`, invoice SHA-256 `ad826c82…3e4c1`), the complex bill fails at the admitted BIT saving `C = 17/5000` by exactly **72.892623830207**, or **4.049590212789 per FULL**. Every local paid job and local helper target appears exactly 18 times, once per FULL. With all other paid work and targets fixed:

| Local change per FULL | Passes at 17/5000? |
|---|---|
| delete one paid job of rank ≤ 4 | no (rank 4 gives 3.98) |
| delete one paid job of rank 5, 6 or 7 | yes |
| fewest deletions using only rank ≤ 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 | 5 / 3 / 2 / 2 |
| free full refinement of rank-9 helpers into rank-1 targets | needs 61 of 412 |
| free balanced 4+5 split of rank-9 helpers | needs 194 of 412 |
| refine every local helper target fully | first crossing in [0.0094772838495, 0.0094772838496] |
| the same at `C = 1/100` | **fails** |

Full refinement maximizes a helper's target moment at every `C`, since `Σ p^(1-C) ≤ r` for any partition of `r`. So **no split of local helper targets alone, with paid work fixed, lets the selected invoice pass at 1/100.** For comparison, #5599 refines 13 helpers, and #5702 needs 15 fully refined H9 sources to fund one added H1 per FULL.

## Evidence and reproduction

`verify.py` checks the invoice bytes against the exporter's hash and the 18-fold replication. It evaluates every `r^(1-C)` with correctly rounded 80-digit decimal `ln`/`exp`, so the total error is far below `1e-50` and every sign clears `1e-30`. A float evaluation corroborates the deficit. Each boundary case is rerun on the actual changed invoice: rank 4 versus 5, 4 versus 5 rank-one deletions, 60 versus 61 and 193 versus 194 H9 splits, and the `1/100` failure.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -B -W error research/selected-invoice-bit-cap-thresholds/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -B -W error research/selected-invoice-bit-cap-thresholds/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-invoice-bit-cap-thresholds
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/selected-invoice-bit-cap-thresholds --check-source-history
```

Local results: both verifier runs print `PASS_SELECTED_INVOICE_BIT_CAP_THRESHOLDS` in about 0.2 s, `research_package.py` prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE … outcome=completed` in 0.65 s, and `check_research_commit.py` prints `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` at `d9d9f7c66`. On a full checkout, `export_selected_invoice.py` reproduces the packaged invoice hash.

## Limitations

These deletions and splits are free in an optimistic accounting relaxation. No restoration, native alignment, precision, compiler, stock or outer cost is charged, and no physical word is supplied. A passing row keeps a route open. It is not a supplier. Once complex passes at `17/5000`, the admitted BIT saving binds, but this package does not prove the outer κ. It certifies only the signs at the stated `C` values and the root bracket. Uniqueness of the refined crossing is not claimed beyond the separate failure at `1/100`. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

1. Which physical window of the selected local word can delete one paid job of rank 5, 6 or 7, or two of rank 3 or 4, while keeping every target and restoration? Under this accounting, any one of them lets complex pass at the admitted BIT saving.
2. Helper splitting alone stops below `1/100`. Which paid-side or main-target changes, priced with the same moment, would let complex pass at `1/100`? A target above `.0034` also needs BIT improvement.

## Related open work

- #5999: saves P104 scalar units through dirty-output sharing. That is scalar work, not the paid histogram priced here.
- #5975 and #5994: study the successor #5907 word, not the selected #5599 invoice. I did not compute their invoices.
- #5606 and #5553: propose P104 helper-split κ values on other words. Those are distinct invoices; no number is compared.
- #5932: finds the minimum number of cross-side paid-job merges (406) that let the frozen #5298 joint BIT/complex ledger pass at `C = 7/2000`. It uses the same signed moment test at a fixed C, but on a different ledger and at a different C. This PR computes nothing at `7/2000` on that ledger, so no number is compared.
- #5992: certifies the moment ceiling of the pooled R437 carrier profile (crossing near 0.00173678297) and shows `17/5000` is unreachable there. It uses the same kind of fixed-C moment test, and also tests at `17/5000`, but on a different invoice. This PR's deficit at `17/5000` is for the selected #5599 P104 invoice only, so no number is compared.
- Other open PRs from this account opened since the CLAIM (#6001–#6009, #6011) study different objects and do not price this invoice.
